question: IA
answer:
# Qualifications for Inspection Authorization (IA) with Respect to Major Alterations

## 0. Bottom line

- **The qualification standard is 14 CFR § 65.91** (Title 14, Chapter I, Subchapter D, Part 65, Subpart D — Mechanics). It contains **five** eligibility criteria at § 65.91(c)(1) through (c)(5).
- **The authority that actually touches major alterations is 14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1)** (Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations). Qualifications alone authorize nothing; § 65.91 makes you eligible, § 65.95 says what you may approve.
- **Prerequisite credential:** a currently effective mechanic certificate with **both** an airframe rating **and** a powerplant rating, each currently effective and **in effect for a total of at least 3 years** — § 65.91(c)(1). A mechanic holding only one rating cannot qualify.
- **Major alterations appear explicitly only twice in the IA scheme:** (a) as the subject of the written test — § 65.91(c)(5), "returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations"; and (b) as the privilege itself — § 65.95(a)(1), which permits the IA holder to inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft or related part/appliance after a **major repair or major alteration only if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**.
- **The IA is not a design approval.** An IA cannot make a major alteration approvable; the approved technical data must already exist (STC, FAA-approved data, or a field-approved data package). The IA's act is inspection and return-to-service approval, not data approval.
- **Classification is a separate question** governed by the § 1.1 definition and Appendix A to Part 43, not by Part 65.

## 1. Scope statement (assumptions, stated plainly)

The request did not specify which of several possible readings was intended. This answer adopts the reading that is standard for AMT/IA study and for Part 43 compliance work:

- "Inspection auth" = **Inspection Authorization under 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D** (§§ 65.91–65.95).
- "Major alterations" = the regulatory term defined in **14 CFR § 1.1** and elaborated in **Appendix A to Part 43**.
- Aircraft in scope = aircraft with a **U.S. standard airworthiness certificate** maintained under Part 43/Part 91. Aircraft excluded from Part 43 by § 43.1(b) (notably most experimental-certificated aircraft) and aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program (§§ 121.367, 135.411(a)(2)) fall outside parts of this framework; see § 7 below.
- Source of law = **current eCFR text of Title 14**, per the requester's pointer to ecfr.gov. Where a paragraph letter or revision level is uncertain, it is flagged rather than asserted.

If the requester actually meant "who may approve a major alteration on a Part 145 repair station's work" or "who may approve a major alteration on a Part 121 aircraft," the answer changes — see § 7.

## 2. Regulatory map

| Question | Governing citation |
|---|---|
| Am I eligible for an IA? | 14 CFR § 65.91 (esp. (c)(1)–(5)) |
| What may an IA approve? | 14 CFR § 65.95(a) |
| What may an IA **not** approve? | 14 CFR § 65.95(b) |
| How does the IA stay current? | 14 CFR §§ 65.92 (duration), 65.93 (renewal) |
| Who may *perform* a major alteration? | 14 CFR § 43.3 |
| Who may *approve for return to service*? | 14 CFR §§ 43.5, 43.7 (IA route cross-references § 65.95) |
| What records are required? | 14 CFR § 43.9 (FAA Form 337 for major repairs/alterations); § 43.11 for inspections |
| Is it "major"? | 14 CFR § 1.1; Appendix A to Part 43 |
| What data must be used? | 14 CFR §§ 43.13(a)–(b); § 65.95(a)(1) (approved technical data) |

## 3. The qualifications — 14 CFR § 65.91

§ 65.91(a) requires application on the form and in the manner prescribed by the Administrator (FAA Form 8610-1, Mechanic's Application for Inspection Authorization; processed through IACRA/FSDO — verify current form revision). § 65.91(b) entitles an applicant who meets the section to an IA. The substantive qualifications are § 65.91(c):

> **(c) To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—**
> **(1)** Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;
> **(2)** Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;
> **(3)** Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;
> **(4)** Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and
> **(5)** Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter.

**How each criterion bears on major alterations:**

| # | Criterion | Citation | Bearing on major alterations |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A&P mechanic certificate, both ratings, in effect ≥ 3 years | § 65.91(c)(1) | Establishes the breadth of airframe *and* powerplant competence; a major alteration frequently spans both. The 3-year clock runs on the ratings, not on alteration experience. |
| 2 | Actively engaged ≥ 2 years before application in maintaining aircraft certificated/maintained under the chapter | § 65.91(c)(2) | This is the practical-experience gate. It is a 2-year lookback that runs in parallel with — not after — the 3-year rating requirement in (c)(1). |
| 3 | Fixed base of operations, reachable in person or by telephone during a normal working week | § 65.91(c)(3) | Supports the FSDO's ability to contact the IA about approvals, including alteration approvals. The base need not be where authority is exercised. |
| 4 | Equipment, facilities, and inspection data available to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, related parts/appliances | § 65.91(c)(4) | Directly relevant: an IA cannot approve a major alteration without access to the inspection data needed to verify conformity to approved technical data. |
| 5 | Pass a written test covering inspection to safety standards for return to service after **major repairs and major alterations**, and annual/progressive inspections under Part 43 | § 65.91(c)(5) | This is the **only** place in § 65.91 where major alterations are named. There is no separate "major alteration hours" eligibility minimum. |

**Point to state clearly:** § 65.91 imposes **no minimum number of major alterations performed or inspected**. Major-alteration competency is tested at (c)(5) and demonstrated later through the approval act itself under § 65.95 and the record under § 43.9.

## 4. The privilege — 14 CFR § 65.95 (paraphrased; pull verbatim text from eCFR before publishing)

- **§ 65.95(a)(1)** — the holder may inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance after a **major repair or major alteration**, in accordance with Part 43, **if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**. The privilege expressly does **not** extend to aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program under §§ 121.367 and 135.411(a)(2).
- **§ 65.95(a)(2)** — annual inspection, and performance or supervision of a progressive inspection, per §§ 43.11, 43.12, and 91.409.
- **§ 65.95(b)** — limitations. The controlling limitation for this question: an IA may not approve for return to service work that was **not** done in accordance with FAA-approved technical data. The IA's signature certifies conformity and airworthiness, not the adequacy of the design.

**Practical consequence:** the IA's review is a two-part test — (1) is there Administrator-approved technical data covering this alteration? and (2) was the work accomplished in conformity with that data? If either answer is no, the IA has no authority to sign it off.

## 5. Is it actually a "major" alteration?

- **§ 1.1** defines major alteration (and major repair) by reference to type design change or effect on weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness.
- **Appendix A to Part 43** provides the enumerated lists of major alterations and major repairs, plus the preventive-maintenance list.
- A minor alteration, by contrast, may be approved for return to service under § 43.7 by a certificated mechanic who performed it; the IA is not required. Getting the classification wrong is the single most common error in this area.

## 6. The Part 43 sign-off chain around an IA approval

1. **§ 43.3** — who may perform the alteration (certificated mechanic with appropriate ratings, repair station, air carrier, manufacturer, etc.). Note: performing a major alteration does **not** require an IA.
2. **§ 43.13(a)–(b)** — work must be done by methods/techniques/practices acceptable to the Administrator and to at least the original or properly altered condition; must use FAA-approved data where the alteration is major.
3. **§ 43.9** — maintenance record entry; for major repairs and major alterations the **FAA Form 337** requirement applies (commonly cited as § 43.9(d) — verify the paragraph letter against current eCFR), with instructions in the AC 43.9-1 series (verify current revision).
4. **§§ 43.5 and 43.7** — approval for return to service, and the persons authorized to give it; § 43.7 includes the IA-holder route that cross-references § 65.95.
5. **§ 43.11** — inspection record entries (annual/progressive), separate from alteration records.

## 7. Alternative routes of approval (why the IA answer is not universal)

- **Part 145 repair stations** — approve work within their ratings and limitations under their FAA-accepted repair station/quality control manual and Part 145 privileges; an IA is not the vehicle for a repair station's return-to-service approval.
- **Part 121/135 aircraft under a CAMP** — expressly carved out of § 65.95(a)(1); approval flows through the operator's maintenance program.
- **Design/data approval** — Part 21 (e.g., STC under Part 21 Subpart E) or FAA field approval of data; AC 43-210A series (verify current revision) describes standardized field-approval request procedures for major repairs/alterations.
- **Experimental/other excluded aircraft** — § 43.1(b) excludes certain aircraft (notably most experimental-certificated) from Part 43, so the Part 43/IA framework described above does not apply to them as written.

## 8. Currency and renewal (secondary — verify exact figures on eCFR)

- **§ 65.92** — duration of an inspection authorization (fixed renewal cycle).
- **§ 65.93** — renewal; the holder must show one of several activity options within the preceding 12 months. One option is performing **at least two major repairs or major alterations** during that period. Because this figure is from secondary/AMT-level material rather than the quoted primary text I hold, treat it as "verify against § 65.93 before relying on it"; the qualification standard itself (§ 65.91) does not depend on it.

## 9. Note on the "FAA-AMT" reference

FAA-AMT material (the FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician handbooks, FAA-H-8083-30/-31/-32 series, and the faa.gov/mechanics IA resources, including the IA knowledge test guide, AC 65-33 series — verify current revision) is a **secondary** summary of Part 65 and Part 43. It is appropriate for study and for orientation, but for a compliance determination the controlling text is 14 CFR. Where AMT material and the current eCFR text diverge, eCFR controls; AMT handbooks lag rulemaking.

## 10. Common errors to avoid

1. **Confusing qualification with privilege.** § 65.91 makes you eligible; § 65.95 grants authority. Quoting only § 65.91 leaves the major-alteration question unanswered.
2. **Assuming an IA is required to *perform* a major alteration.** It is not; a certificated A&P may perform it under § 43.3. The IA enters at return-to-service approval.
3. **Assuming an IA can approve the *data*.** Only the Administrator approves technical data; the IA verifies conformity to it (§ 65.95(a)(1)).
4. **Assuming a single rating suffices.** § 65.91(c)(1) requires both airframe and powerplant.
5. **Treating the 3-year and 2-year requirements as sequential.** They are separate and run in parallel.
6. **Applying the IA framework to CAMP aircraft or excluded aircraft.** See §§ 65.95(a)(1), 43.1(b).

## 11. Verification protocol (how a reviewer confirms every citation)

1. Open `https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D` and confirm the text of §§ 65.91, 65.92, 65.93, 65.95.
2. Open `https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-43` and confirm §§ 43.1, 43.3, 43.5, 43.7, 43.9, 43.11, 43.13.
3. Confirm Appendix A to Part 43 and the § 1.1 definitions.
4. Record the eCFR "current as of" date and the amendment numbers for Parts 1, 43, and 65 on the face of any published answer.
5. Any paragraph letter flagged above (notably § 43.9(d) for Form 337 and the § 43.7 IA paragraph) must be re-checked against the live text before the citation is published.

## 12. Sources

- 14 CFR § 65.91 — https://ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.91 (retrieved 2026-11-14T18:07:34Z; sha256 8dd2b52b76db; text of § 65.91(c) quoted above is verbatim from this retrieval)
- 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D — http://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D
- 14 CFR § 65.93 — http://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.93
- 14 CFR Part 65 (2025 ed., vol. 2) — https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title14-vol2/pdf/CFR-2025-title14-vol2-part65-subpartD.pdf
- 14 CFR Part 43 (2025 ed., vol. 1) — https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title14-vol1/pdf/CFR-2025-title14-vol1-part43.pdf

**Answer to the ask, restated:** the qualifications for inspection authorization with respect to major alterations are set by **14 CFR § 65.91**, specifically the five criteria at § 65.91(c)(1)–(5) — A&P certificate with both ratings in effect at least 3 years; at least 2 years of active engagement in maintaining aircraft under the chapter immediately before application; a fixed base of operations with telephone access during a normal working week; available equipment, facilities, and inspection data; and passage of a written test covering inspection to safety standards for return to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual/progressive inspections under Part 43 — with the resulting authority to approve major alterations for return to service governed by **14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1)**, limited to work accomplished in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator, and recorded per **14 CFR § 43.9** (FAA Form 337).

question: IA
answer:
# FAA Inspection Authorization (IA) — Qualifications Applicable to Major Alterations

Source of authority: 14 CFR as published on eCFR (Title 14, Chapter I, Subchapter D). Cross-referenced to FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician (FAA-AMT) handbook material and FAA guidance. Verified text quoted in Section 4; unverified citations are flagged in Section 10.

**Scope statement (single assumption):** U.S. federal civil aviation, 14 CFR only; 'major alteration' as defined in 14 CFR 1.1 and listed in Appendix A to Part 43; the question is about *personnel qualifications*, not the airworthiness standards of the alteration itself. 'FAA-AMT' is read as the FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook series and related FAA AMT training material — these are training references that *summarize* the regulations and are not themselves regulatory authority.

---

## 1. Short answer

The question actually contains two separate regulatory questions, and they have different answers:

| # | Question | Governing rule | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Who is qualified to **perform/supervise** a major alteration? | 14 CFR 43.3; 65.81; 65.83 | A certificated mechanic holding the rating appropriate to the item worked on (airframe or powerplant), a certificated repairman, a certificated repair station, or a person working under the supervision of one of these; subject to the 24-month recent-experience requirement. |
| Q2 | Who is qualified to **inspect and approve a major alteration for return to service**? | 14 CFR 43.5; 43.7; **65.91(c)** (eligibility); **65.95(a)(1)** (privilege) | The holder of an **Inspection Authorization** issued under Part 65 Subpart D, *or* another person/entity authorized by 43.7 (e.g., a repair station within its ratings, or a Part 121/135 certificate holder's authorized personnel under its approved program). |

**The IA qualifications themselves are in 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)–(5)** — five gates, quoted verbatim in Section 4. **The IA's authority to act on a major alteration is in 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1)**, and it carries three conditions (Section 5).

---

## 2. Definitions that drive the answer

| Term | Citation | Effect on the answer |
|---|---|---|
| **Major alteration** | 14 CFR 1.1: an alteration not listed in the aircraft/engine/propeller specifications that (1) might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness; or (2) is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations. Enumerated examples in **Appendix A to Part 43**. | Triggers the IA/approved-data path. A *minor* alteration does not. |
| **Major repair** | 14 CFR 1.1; Appendix A to Part 43. | Parallel rule; the IA privilege in 65.95(a)(1) covers major repairs and major alterations in the same sentence. |
| **Technical data approved by the Administrator** | Referenced in 65.95(a)(1) and 43.7. | This is the *condition* on the IA's approval, not a qualification of the IA. It is satisfied by an STC, a field approval, a DER/DAS-approved repair or alteration document, or other FAA-approved data — **not** by the IA's own judgment. |

---

## 3. Do not conflate the three distinct authorities

A major alteration touches three separate approvals. Only the middle one is the IA's.

**3.1 Performing the work — 14 CFR 43.3; 65.81; 65.83**
- 43.3: no person may perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, or alteration except as provided; the paragraph list authorizes the holder of a mechanic certificate with the appropriate rating, a certificated repairman, a repair station, an air carrier, and persons working under their supervision.
- 65.81: general privileges and limitations of a mechanic certificate — the mechanic may perform or supervise work on items for which he/she is rated, with the exclusions stated in that section (e.g., major repairs to and major alterations of propellers, and instrument work, are carved out of the mechanic's direct authority).
- 65.83: recent-experience requirement — a mechanic may not exercise the privileges of the certificate and rating unless, within the preceding 24 months, the Administrator has found the holder able to do the work, or the holder has for at least 6 months been engaged in one of the enumerated qualifying activities. **This applies to the IA holder too, because the IA is built on top of a mechanic certificate.**

**3.2 Approving for return to service — 14 CFR 43.5; 43.7; 65.95(a)(1); 145.201**
- 43.5: general rule that no person may return an aircraft to service after maintenance/alteration unless it has been maintained, inspected, and approved by persons authorized under Part 43, and — for aircraft operated under Part 121/125/135 — unless the certificate holder's manual/program is followed (43.5(b)).
- 43.7: the section that enumerates *persons authorized to approve for return to service*, and imposes the record-entry, Form 337, and weight-and-balance/flight-check conditions. **This is the section that decides whether an A&P, an IA, a repair station, or an air carrier may sign off a major alteration.** (Paragraph lettering: see Section 10.)
- 65.95(a)(1): the IA's specific major-repair/major-alteration approval privilege.
- 145.201: privileges of a certificated repair station, including approving for return to service articles it has maintained/altered within the scope of its ratings and operations specifications.

**3.3 Approving the design/technical data — Part 21; Part 183**
- An STC (Part 21 subpart E), a field approval issued by the FAA, a DER/DAS approval (Part 183), or a PMA authorizes the *data*.
- **An IA has no authority to approve design data.** The IA's signature says "the work conforms to FAA-approved data and the item is airworthy" — it does not say "this alteration is an approved design." This is the single most common error in IA-privilege questions.

---

## 4. IA eligibility — 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)–(5) (verbatim, verified)

> "To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—
> (1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;
> (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;
> (3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;
> (4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and
> (5) Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter."

### 4.1 Compliance checklist (what an applicant must be able to document)

| Gate | Requirement | Evidence to hold | Common failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 65.91(c)(1) | Mechanic certificate, **both** Airframe and Powerplant ratings, currently effective, each in effect **at least 3 years** | Certificate (front and back), issuance dates for each rating | Applying with only one rating; ratings held less than 3 years; lapsed certificate |
| 65.91(c)(2) | **Actively engaged for at least the 2 years before application** in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR | Employer letters, work orders, training records, logbook/337 sign-offs covering the 2-year window | Counting non-aviation mechanical work; counting work on non-14 CFR (e.g., foreign or military-only) aircraft without 14 CFR-maintained experience; gaps |
| 65.91(c)(3) | Fixed base of operations, reachable in person or by telephone during a normal working week | Written statement of address/phone | Believing the base must be where the IA actually works — the rule expressly says it need not be |
| 65.91(c)(4) | Equipment, facilities, and inspection data available | Inventory list; subscriptions to current inspection data (e.g., manufacturer maintenance manuals, AD/ICA access) | Owning tools but no current inspection data for the product types to be inspected |
| 65.91(c)(5) | Pass the FAA written test on inspecting to safety standards for RTS after **major repairs and major alterations** and for annual and progressive inspections under Part 43 | FAA test report | Assuming the A&P oral/practical substitutes for it |

**Note on gate (5):** the test is specifically scoped to return-to-service after **major repairs and major alterations** plus annual/progressive inspections. That is the regulatory hook that makes the IA — and not the plain A&P — the default major-alteration approver.

**Note on form and filing:** application is made to the FAA (Flight Standards District Office having jurisdiction) on the prescribed form, per 65.91(a)–(b); the certificate itself is issued under Part 65 Subpart D. Duration and renewal are governed by 65.92/65.93 (biennial cycle, with the renewal-eligibility activities listed in 65.93).

---

## 5. The IA privilege for major alterations — 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1), and its three conditions

As stated in FAA guidance (AC 20-62E, reflecting 65.95(a)(1)):

> "Inspection Authorization (IA). May inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except aircraft maintained in accordance with a Continuous Airworthiness Maintenance Program (CAMP) under part 121 or 135) after a major repair or alteration as provided in part 43 if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator."

Read as three cumulative conditions plus one exclusion:

| Condition | Text | Practical meaning |
|---|---|---|
| C1 — Scope | "any aircraft or related part or appliance" | Airframe, engine, propeller, appliance, component. |
| C2 — Exclusion | "except aircraft maintained in accordance with a CAMP under part 121 or 135" | For CAMP aircraft, return to service is by the certificate holder's authorized personnel under its approved program, not by an independent IA. See Section 7. |
| C3 — Data | "if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator" | The alteration must have been accomplished per FAA-approved data. If the data is only *acceptable* (not approved), the IA cannot approve RTS. |
| C4 — Process | "as provided in part 43" | The Part 43 record, Form 337, and weight/balance or flight-check requirements must be satisfied (Section 6). |

The IA privilege also covers annual and progressive inspections under 65.95(a)(2) — relevant context but **not** part of the major-alteration answer.

**Independence:** the regulation does not, by its terms, bar an IA from approving for return to service an alteration the IA personally performed. Where independence is required (Part 121/135 programs, repair station manuals/OpSpecs, some Part 91 operator programs), that requirement comes from the operator's approved manual, not from 65.95.

---

## 6. Documentation chain — the approval is only valid if this is complete

| Step | Requirement | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Work performed by an authorized person | 43.3; 65.81; 65.83 |
| 2 | Work performed in accordance with FAA-approved technical data (STC, field approval, DER/DAS, etc.) | 65.95(a)(1); 43.7 |
| 3 | Maintenance record entry — description of work, date, name, certificate number/type | 43.9(a) |
| 4 | **FAA Form 337** executed for the major repair or major alteration | 43.9 and Appendix B to Part 43 (paragraph designator flagged, Section 10) |
| 5 | If the alteration changes weight/balance or flight characteristics — aircraft weighed or flight checked, results entered in the records | 43.7 |
| 6 | Approval for return to service by an authorized person (IA, repair station, or certificate holder's authorized personnel) | 43.5; 43.7; 65.95(a)(1); 145.201 |
| 7 | Records retained and made available | 91.417 (operator records); 43.9 record content |

Appendix B to Part 43 is the recording rule for major repairs and major alterations — it governs *how* the entry and Form 337 are made, and is the correct citation when someone asks "where does it say Form 337 is required for a major alteration?"

---

## 7. Part 121 / Part 135 and CAMP aircraft — the exclusion in practice

- 43.5(b): for aircraft operated under Part 121, 125, or 135, the certificate holder's manual/program governs, and return to service is by that holder's authorized personnel.
- 121.709 (airworthiness release or aircraft log entry) and 135.443 (airworthiness release) are the operator-side return-to-service instruments.
- Consequence: an independent IA **cannot** approve a major alteration for return to service on an aircraft maintained under a Part 121 or 135 CAMP. The IA can still inspect; the approval authority sits with the certificate holder.

---

## 8. FAA-AMT cross-reference map (training material, not authority)

Use these only as the teaching layer over the citations above; every substantive statement in them traces back to Part 43 or Part 65.

| FAA-AMT reference | What it covers on this topic | Regulatory basis it summarizes |
|---|---|---|
| AMT Handbook — General (FAA-H-8083-30 series), chapters on maintenance/repair and on maintenance forms and records | Mechanic privileges and limitations; major vs. minor alteration; Form 337; record entries | 43.3; 43.7; 43.9; Appendix A and B to Part 43; 65.81; 65.83 |
| AMT Handbook — Airframe (FAA-H-8083-31 series) and Powerplant (FAA-H-8083-32 series), maintenance/records and inspection chapters | Where the airframe/powerplant rating boundary falls; inspection and RTS entries | 43.3; 43.7; 65.85; 65.87 |
| FAA IA guidance (AC 20-62E, IA renewal/preparation material, FAASTeam AMT seminars) | The IA privilege statement quoted in Section 5; CAMP exclusion; approved-data condition | 65.91; 65.93; 65.95(a)(1) |
| FAA Order 8900.1 (Flight Standards Information Management System) | Field approval process for major alterations where no STC exists | Part 21; Part 43 — **section-level citation to be confirmed** (Section 10) |

---

## 9. Traps — the answers that are wrong

1. **"Any A&P can approve a major alteration for return to service."** Wrong as stated. The mechanic's RTS authority for a major repair or alteration under 43.7 is conditioned on the work having been done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and the CAMP exclusion applies.
2. **"The IA approves the alteration."** Wrong. The IA approves the *work* for return to service. The *design/data* is approved by the FAA (field approval), an STC, or a DER/DAS under Part 183.
3. **"An IA needs a type rating / a degree / a specific number of years beyond the mechanic certificate."** Wrong. The only time gates are the 3-year rating currency and the 2-year active-engagement period in 65.91(c)(1)–(2).
4. **"A mechanic with only an Airframe rating (or only Powerplant) can hold an IA."** Wrong — 65.91(c)(1) requires **both** ratings.
5. **"The fixed base must be where the IA does inspections."** Wrong — 65.91(c)(3) says expressly it need not be.
6. **"The IA never expires."** Wrong — 65.92/65.93 provide a biennial cycle with defined renewal-eligibility activities.
7. **"An A&P can sign an annual inspection."** Wrong — annual and progressive inspections require an IA under 65.95(a)(2).
8. **"Part 121 CAMP aircraft can be signed off by any IA."** Wrong — express exclusion in 65.95(a)(1).

---

## 10. Currency and verification status

**Verified from fetched source text:** 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)–(5), quoted verbatim in Section 4 (eCFR, Part 65 Subpart D); the IA privilege statement in Section 5 (AC 20-62E, which restates 65.95(a)(1)).

**To be confirmed against the current eCFR text before publication of any compliance document:**
1. **43.7 paragraph designators.** The section is the correct citation for "persons authorized to approve for return to service" and for the record/Form 337/weight-and-balance conditions, but the individual paragraph letters (a)–(h) shift between amendments and are deliberately **not** asserted here. Quote the section, not a letter, until the current text is pulled.

answer:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) Qualifications as They Bear on Major Alterations
14 CFR reference brief — Regulatory Specialist deliverable

## 1. Answer in brief

An Inspection Authorization is issued under **14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D (Mechanics), §§65.91–65.95**. The qualifications are in **§65.91(c)** — five elements, all mandatory. The major-alteration content of the question is *not* in §65.91; it sits in **§65.95(a)(1)** (what the IA may approve and the 'approved data' limit), read with **§43.5 and §43.7** (approval for return to service), **Appendix A to Part 43** (what makes an alteration major), and **Appendix B to Part 43** (Form 337 recording and submission).

So: the *qualification* is §65.91(c); the *authority over major alterations* is §65.95(a)(1) + Part 43; the *maintenance of the qualification* is §65.92/§65.93. A holder must satisfy all three to lawfully approve a major alteration for return to service.

## 2. Governing rule set

| Layer | Citation | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| Eligibility to hold an IA | 14 CFR 65.91 | The five qualifications + application + written test |
| Duration of the IA | 14 CFR 65.92 | Expiration cycle |
| Renewal of the IA | 14 CFR 65.93 | Recent activity or refresher course |
| Privileges/limits of the IA | 14 CFR 65.95 | What the IA may and may not approve, incl. major alterations |
| Who may return to service | 14 CFR 43.5, 43.7 | Return-to-service conditions and authorized persons |
| Record content | 14 CFR 43.9, 91.417 | Maintenance record entries and retention |
| What is 'major' | 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A | Major alteration / major repair definitions |
| Recording majors | 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix B | Form 337 execution and submission |
| Mechanic prerequisite | 14 CFR 65.71–65.83 | A&P certificate that must precede the IA |

## 3. §65.91(c) — the five IA qualifications (verbatim from current eCFR text)

> (c) To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—
> (1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;
> (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;
> (3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;
> (4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and
> (5) Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter.

How each element is normally evidenced:

| # | Element | Practical evidence |
|---|---|---|
| (1) | Mechanic certificate with **both** Airframe and Powerplant ratings, currently effective, **in effect for a total of at least 3 years** | Certificate; the 3 years is a *total*, not necessarily continuous — do not read it as 3 unbroken years |
| (2) | **Actively engaged** for at least the **2-year period** before application in maintaining aircraft certificated/maintained under 14 CFR | Employment/engagement record, logbook, employer letters. Distinct from the 3-year certificate element — they are two separate clocks |
| (3) | **Fixed base of operations**, reachable in person or by telephone during a normal working week | Address/contact on the application; need not be where the IA works |
| (4) | **Equipment, facilities, and inspection data** available | Tooling, current technical data/subscriptions, inspection references |
| (5) | **Written test** on inspecting to safety standards for return to service after major repairs and major alterations, and annual/progressive inspections under Part 43 | Airman knowledge test result. The test content is defined by §65.91(c)(5); test length/passing score are set outside the regulation — verify against the current FAA IA knowledge test guide rather than assuming figures |

Application mechanics: §65.91(a)–(b) provide that application is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator (in practice FAA Form 8610-1, Mechanic's Application for Inspection Authorization) and that an applicant meeting the section is entitled to the authorization. Confirm current form edition and filing channel before use.

## 4. What 'regarding major alterations' actually requires

### 4.1 The major/minor gate
Whether an IA is needed at all is decided first by **Appendix A to Part 43**, which defines major alterations (and major repairs) by category — airframe, powerplant, propeller, appliance — plus the catch-all for alterations that appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other airworthiness qualities. If the alteration is **minor**, no IA approval is required; it may be returned to service by an appropriately rated mechanic under §43.7. If it is **major**, the IA (or other authorized approver) is required, and the approved-data rule applies.

### 4.2 The approved-data rule — the heart of IA authority over major alterations
**§65.95(a)(1)** permits the IA to inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft, airframe, engine, propeller, appliance, or component part after a **major repair or major alteration only if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator.** Correspondingly, §65.95(b) prohibits the IA from approving such work where the data is not FAA-approved.

The operative distinction an IA must apply:
- **Approved data** — e.g., data approved with an STC, TC/type design data, AD-mandated data, or a specific FAA field approval. This is what supports an IA signature.
- **Acceptable data** — e.g., AC 43.13-2B generic methods, manufacturer's generic maintenance instructions, standard practice. Acceptable data supports *minor* alterations and *major repairs/alterations only where the data is itself approved for that application*; it does **not** by itself authorize an IA to approve a major alteration.

Consequence: an IA cannot convert an unapproved major alteration into an approved one by inspecting it. If the alteration is major and no approved data exists, the **data** must be approved first — normally by FAA field approval (Form 337, Block 3) or by STC/design approval — and that approval function is outside the IA's authority. FAA Order 8300.16 and the AC 43-2xx series are the advisory material to consult for the field-approval path; they are guidance, not the rule.

### 4.3 Recording and submission — Appendix B to Part 43
A major repair or major alteration is recorded on **FAA Form 337**. The form is executed by the person performing the work, and the **return-to-service approval is signed in Block 7** by the IA (or other person authorized under §43.7); Block 3 is the FAA approval block used for field approval. A copy goes to the aircraft owner and a copy is submitted to the FAA (local office) within the period stated in Appendix B and on the form — the familiar figure is 48 hours after approval for return to service, but confirm the current text and form instructions before relying on the number.

### 4.4 What an IA may not do on a major alteration
- May not approve work performed without FAA-approved technical data (§65.95).
- May not substitute acceptable data for approved data.
- May not use the signature as a design approval; the IA certifies inspection and conformity to approved data, not the adequacy of a new design.
- May not act outside the equipment/facilities/inspection-data capability required by §65.91(c)(4).
- The privilege is personal: the IA inspects and approves; it is not a supervisory or delegable approval.

### 4.5 Related return-to-service and record conditions
§43.5 conditions return-to-service approval on the maintenance record entry (§43.9 or §43.11), execution of the repair/alteration form, and — where the alteration changes operating limitations or approved flight manual data — appropriate revision of those limitations (§91.9). §91.417 governs retention and transfer of records of major alterations. An IA signature without the §43.9 entry and the revised limitations/W&B is an incomplete approval.

## 5. Keeping the qualification — duration and renewal

- **§65.92 (Duration):** an inspection authorization expires on **March 31 of each odd-numbered year** — a two-year cycle. (Paraphrase; verify exact wording.)
- **§65.93 (Renewal):** renewal requires, within the **90-day period before** applying, one of: at least one **annual inspection** performed; or at least **two major repairs or major alterations** performed; or at least one **progressive inspection** performed or supervised; or successful completion of an FAA-accepted **refresher course** (commonly 8 hours). (Substance paraphrased — confirm the current paragraph lettering and course-hour figure in §65.93 before quoting.)
- If the authorization is allowed to lapse, the holder generally must re-establish eligibility under §65.91, including the written test. Verify the lapse/reinstatement provisions of §65.93 before advising a specific individual.

Note the deliberate point for the AMT audience: the **two major alterations** used to renew are a *renewal activity* test, not a qualification; do not conflate it with the §65.91(c)(2) two-year engagement element or the §65.91(c)(1) three-year certificate element.

## 6. The 'FAA-AMT' pathway (why the tag matters)

The IA is not a stand-alone entry credential — it sits on top of the mechanic certificate. The chain for an aviation maintenance technician is:

1. **Mechanic certificate** — §65.71 (eligibility: age, English, etc.), §65.75 (knowledge test), §65.77 (experience: 18 months for a single rating, or 30 months concurrently for both A and P), §65.79 (oral and practical). Training may be obtained through a Part 147 AMTS or on-the-job; an authenticated Part 147 document evidences eligibility to test for the rating(s) covered by the completed curriculum.
2. **Both ratings in effect for a total of at least 3 years**, plus 2 years actively engaged (§65.91(c)(1)–(2)).
3. **IA written test** and application (§65.91(a), (c)(5)).

A mechanic certificate alone does not authorize major-alteration approval; §65.81 privileges are subject to the major repair/alteration exclusions and §43.7 conditions. The IA is the credential that unlocks the major-alteration approval.

## 7. Practical checklist an IA applies before signing a major alteration

1. Is it **major** under Appendix A to Part 43? If not, no IA approval is needed.
2. Is there **FAA-approved technical data** covering the alteration (STC, TC data, AD, field approval)? If not, stop — route to field approval.
3. Was the work **performed in accordance with** that data (conformity, not just resemblance)?
4. Does the IA hold the **equipment, facilities, and inspection data** required by §65.91(c)(4) for this specific inspection?
5. Is the **§43.9 record entry** complete?
6. Are **operating limitations / AFM data / weight and balance** revised per §43.5 and §91.9?
7. Is **Form 337** executed, Block 7 signed, owner copy delivered, FAA copy submitted per Appendix B?
8. Is the IA's own authorization **current** (§65.92) and has renewal activity been maintained (§65.93)?
